summary: Steel lookout built 1922 on Tussey Mountain at Lytle's Knob (the Loop), 60 ft per 1922-24 notices; sources disagree on county; current condition not documented.

events.note: Steel tower completed the week before a November 7, 1922 notice; 60 feet high on the Loop spur of Tussey Mountain at Lytle's Knob
Eugene Bradley newly appointed tower man; transferred from the Greenwood Fire Tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1922 and 1924 newspaper notices both say 60 feet, which matches the record's 18.3 m; the unsourced 78-foot figure on The Loop page is not used.

The Lytle's Knob page lists Huntingdon County and The Loop page lists Blair County; State Game Lands 118 spans both counties, so the record's Blair County is not contradicted by the land, but the sources conflict.

sources.title: Lytles Knob (Loop), with 1922 and 1924 newspaper clippings

notes_for_editor: History of the 1922 steel tower is well supported by two 1922-24 newspaper notices, but both come through one Forest Lookouts page. The Loop page's 78-foot figure is unsourced. The PA ArcGIS storymap cache (data/raw/pa_storymap/data.json) credits the Blaw-Knox Company, says 60 feet and Blair County on SGL 118, and says it overlooks Huntingdon; it is script-only and fetch_text cannot read it, so it is not cited. No source found describes current condition, standing status or climbing rules; the record's 'standing' is unverified. Access left out of facts for that reason. The Huntingdon/Blair county conflict is unresolved.
